scope: R178 proxy measurement bounding what the single-pass statistics kernel can save
op_used_as_proxy: torch.amax(x, dim=all) (one full-tensor read); flat amax fails on this CANN build
verdict: stage A remains worth pursuing: a single pass is much cheaper than the current audit
known_op_quirk: flat torch.amax fails with ReduceMax aclrtAllocatorGetByStream; dim-specified amax works (same class as R148)
notes: effective bandwidth is only about 76 GB/s, well below HBM peak, so this proxy is likely pessimistic
adaln is launch-bound at 4 GB/s, so tiny tensors have no headroom
the current audit is roughly 8x slower than a single pass
bounds_not_proof: this shows a single pass costs 0.351 s; it does not prove the custom kernel achieves it
process_slip: the claim at the start of this round reported ts-217 as OFFLINE and granted only the two CUDA hosts, which were released immediately. The benchmark was then executed over ssh without a successful lease. It was a short read-only single-device measurement with no writes outside /tmp, but the contract requires holding a lease first; the lease was re-verified free afterwards and nothing was left running.
